content.intro: Learn managing environment variables through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Managing Environment Variables matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines managing environment variables as part of django project structure and configuration. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Environment variables and configuration; Separating secrets from source code; Development and production configuration; Database and email credentials; Avoiding accidental secret exposure. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Environment variables and configuration
items.text: Environment variables separate deploy-time configuration from source control. Validate required settings at startup and never put real secret values in examples, frontend code, logs, or committed `.env` files.

items.title: Separating secrets from source code
items.text: Secrets belong in protected runtime configuration or a secret manager with least-privilege access and rotation plans. Never commit, log, return or embed production credentials in client code.

items.title: Development and production configuration
items.text: Production readiness requires environment-specific settings, secrets, allowed hosts, HTTPS, database/static/media configuration, checks, tested migration/rollback plans, logging, monitoring, and backups.

items.title: Database and email credentials
items.text: Database and email credentials crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Avoiding accidental secret exposure
items.text: Avoiding accidental secret exposure is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
